Next year's iPhone Pro model is expected to adopt an all-new full-glass design to mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone launch. A new leak today detailed Apple's progress on this innovative model.

Here's the latest on Apple's unique iPhone 20 Pro design

The innovative iPhone Ultra (Apple's first foldable model) is set to debut in just a few weeks, but next year will bring another distinctive new iPhone design.

Reports suggest Apple is preparing a special full-glass design for next year's iPhone Pro model. The new device is said to feature a larger display with a quad-curved screen that extends to the edges of the body, achieving a visually borderless effect.

Today, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital updated Apple's progress toward achieving this unique look in a new post.

He stated that the company is using the same glass assembly process previously employed for the iPhone Air, but is making refinements to incorporate more rounded materials.

The post also pointed out improvements in two areas:

  • Thermal performance
  • Body thickness

It remains difficult to determine Apple's target specifications for thickness and design materials at this point. However, all signs so far indicate that this new device will draw inspiration from the iPhone Air and Ultra, but will not prioritize thinness as those two models do.

Based on the latest updates, the new device appears to blend the design innovations of the iPhone Air and Ultra while delivering performance and battery life that meet — or even approach — the expectations of Pro users.

Pro users don't want to sacrifice performance for a slimmer body. But if Apple can release a model that's slightly slimmer, features a distinctive all-glass look, and maintains a comparable user experience, it would be extremely appealing.

How interested are you in next year's rumored iPhone Pro 20 model? Feel free to share in the comments.
